subject: Post-call: Pricing & Latency tradeoffs — token volumes / $/1M target
messages:

Subject: Post-call: Pricing & Latency tradeoffs — token volumes / $/1M target

Thanks for the time today, Jordan — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call: 

What we heard:
- Primary product flow: multi-turn chat assistant in customer dashboard (short prompts + system context + user history).
- Expected volume: looks like 30M–50M tokens/month on initial deployment, with growth to 100M+ over 12 months.
- Peak concurrency: ~15–25 concurrent UI users at peak.
- Latency SLO: target ~250ms p95 for UI responses (ideally under 300ms).
- Cost target: you mentioned a goal around $/1M tokens — please confirm target range.

Redwood short takeaways (high level):
- There is a clear latency vs cost trade-off: Hosted Standard tends to be more cost-efficient but variable p95; Dedicated/reserved capacity gives predictable low p95 at the expense of an infrastructure commit.
- Batch window tuning and KV/prefix caching materially change unit economics for short multi-turn chats. Small batch windows (10–30ms) reduce cost but add tail latency; streaming reduces perceived latency for the user and avoids large batch windows.

Action items / asks from you:
1) Confirm monthly token range (best guess is OK: 30M / 50M / 100M).
2) Confirm target $/1M tokens range you can budget for (ballpark is fine — e.g., $15–$25 / $25–$50).
3) Confirm whether you require an SLA-backed p95 (we can propose Dedicated).

Next steps from our side:
- Rishi will draft a short unit-economics note with 2–3 concrete price options and expected p95 ranges for the workloads you described.
- I’ll share an initial pricing estimate (attached) and a short procurement checklist.

If you can confirm the items above, we’ll prepare a tailored pricing estimate and a short Dedicated trial proposal.

Thanks,

Hi Jordan/Marissa — wanted to provide the concrete unit-economics and latency trade-offs based on the workload you described. I’ll keep it pragmatic: numbers below are estimates and we can run a lightweight benchmark with your prompts to refine.

Assumptions: 3–5 turn chats, avg request/response ~120 tokens generated, model family: open-13B class (quantized).

Estimated pricing bands (per 1M generated tokens):
- Hosted Standard (best-effort batching, shared capacity): ~$28 / 1M tokens — expected p95 300–450ms for short chats (depends on global contention and batching window).
- Hosted Premium (SLA option, priority routing + smaller queues): ~$45–$65 / 1M tokens — expected p95 200–300ms.
- Dedicated Reserved (customer-dedicated GPU pool + caching): ~$14–$22 / 1M tokens (in many commit sizes) — expected p95 ~80–160ms with correct config and warm KV cache. Note: Dedicated requires a monthly capacity commitment which changes invoice structure.

How batching vs streaming affects latency/cost:
- Batching: grouping requests (10–30ms batch window) increases throughput efficiency and lowers per-token infra cost. However it adds batching tail to p95; small windows keep user-perceived latency reasonable.
- Streaming: returns tokens as they are generated — greatly improves perceived latency (users see first tokens quickly) and allows smaller batch windows. Streaming can be combined with modest batching to balance cost/latency.

Practical recommendation for your SLO (250ms p95):
1) Pilot Dedicated with modest commit (e.g., 1–2 gpus equivalent) for the core UI path + streaming enabled. That should hit ~120–200ms p95 and give you $/1M tokens near your $20 target at scale.
2) Use Hosted Standard for lower-priority/async workloads to reduce overall spend.
3) Tune batch window to 10–20ms for the UI path — combined with streaming this keeps perceived latency low while maintaining batching efficiency.

Cost example math: at 40M tokens/month:
- $20 / 1M * 40 = $800 / month in model usage (excluding infra commitments/console fees).
- If you move to Hosted Premium at $45 / 1M, same volume = $1,800 / month.

If helpful, we can run a 2-week Dedicated trial with your prompt set to produce exact p95 curves and a committed pricing proposal. Marissa — I can draft a short benchmarking plan and a recommended commit size for the trial later today.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
